checklist.step: Open a market-entry licensing case for the state and line
actions: Take the launch request from the Insurance Product Manager and record: writing company legal name, NAIC company code, target state, product name, statutory annual statement line, target first-write date.
Open a licensing case in the corporate licensing register and set Status = 'CoA gap analysis'.
Ask the Head of Distribution for the intended distribution footprint so states entered only for a single agency relationship are flagged early.
Attach the signed launch request to the case folder named <company>-<state>-<line>-<target date>.
checklist.done: a licensing case exists carrying company, NAIC co-code, state, statutory line and target first-write date with the launch request attached.

checklist.step: Pull the company's current jurisdiction and lines-of-business grid from the NAIC record
actions: Open the NAIC company record for the writing company and export the Jurisdiction Licensing / State Licensing page showing every state and the lines the company is admitted for.
Export the company demographic page confirming NAIC co-code, FEIN, group code, state of domicile and organisation type.
Save both exports as <company>-naic-jurisdiction-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf into the licensing case folder.
Flag any state where the NAIC grid disagrees with the internal licensing register and raise it to the Regulatory Affairs Manager the same day.
checklist.done: a dated NAIC jurisdiction/lines export sits in the case folder and every disagreement with the internal register is raised.

checklist.step: Map the product to the statutory line codes the CoA must cover
actions: List every coverage the product grants and map each to its statutory annual statement line (for example Line 5.1 Commercial Multiple Peril, Line 19.2 Other Private Passenger Auto Liability, Line 4 Homeowners).
Compare the mapped lines to the state's own CoA line taxonomy, which is often broader or narrower than the annual statement lines.
Where the product bundles coverages across two statutory lines, record both and treat the narrower CoA as the constraint.
Get the mapping confirmed in writing by the Statutory Reporting Manager and file the reply in the case folder.
checklist.done: every coverage in the product maps to a named statutory line and to the state's CoA line taxonomy, confirmed in writing by Statutory Reporting.

checklist.step: Confirm which legal entity will hold the paper in that state
actions: Check the group's entity chart for which writing company is already admitted in the state and for which lines.
Where more than one entity could write, choose on the basis of existing CoA coverage, rate/form approvals already held and surplus capacity.
Confirm with the Chief Financial Officer that the chosen entity's capital and surplus exceed the state's minimum for the requested lines.
Write the chosen entity, its NAIC co-code and the reason for the choice onto the licensing case.
checklist.done: one writing entity is named on the case, with its NAIC co-code and a recorded rationale confirmed against state minimum capital.

checklist.step: Decide CoA present, CoA amendment or full expansion filing
actions: Compare the required line list to the granted line list on the state's CoA certificate held in the register — read the certificate, not the register summary.
Set the case route: NO ACTION (line already granted), AMENDMENT (line addition to an existing CoA), or EXPANSION (company not admitted in the state at all).
For NO ACTION routes, screenshot the certificate line list into the case as the evidence behind the call.
Never close a case on a register field alone — a register row with no attached certificate is treated as no CoA.
checklist.done: the case carries a route decision backed by the actual CoA certificate text, not a register summary field.

checklist.step: Assemble the UCAA Expansion or amendment pack against the state's checklist
actions: Download the current UCAA Expansion Application forms and that state's UCAA state-specific checklist from naic.org, dated on the day of download.

Build the pack: Form 1 Application, Form 2 fee schedule, Form 3 Uniform Consent to Service of Process, Form 5 Lines of Business, Form 11 Plan of Operation, Form 12 pro forma financials, Form 13 Statement of Compliance.
Tick each checklist line to the exhibit that satisfies it and record 'N/A plus reason' where a line does not apply.
Collect the state's own supplements — many states add a producer licensing attestation, an anti-fraud plan and a holding company registration statement.
Save the dated checklist capture as the evidence behind the pack's completeness.
checklist.done: every line of the state's dated UCAA checklist is ticked to a named exhibit or marked N/A with a reason.

checklist.step: Obtain officer and director biographical affidavits with third-party verification
actions: Issue NAIC Form 4 biographical affidavits to every officer and director who must be listed for the state, noting the affidavit must be under 12 months old at submission.
Send each completed affidavit to an NAIC-accepted third-party verification vendor and collect the verification report.
Chase any affidavit with an unexplained employment gap or an undisclosed regulatory action before it goes near the state.
Store affidavits and verification reports in the restricted-access section of the case folder — they carry personal data.
checklist.done: every listed officer and director has a signed affidavit under 12 months old with a completed third-party verification report.

checklist.step: Build the plan of operation and pro forma financial projections
actions: Draft the Form 11 plan of operation: products, target market, distribution channels, projected premium by line, reinsurance programme, claims handling arrangement.
Build the Form 12 pro forma balance sheet, income statement and cash flow for three years, agreeing year one to the approved business plan from FP&A.
Get the Appointed Actuary to confirm the loss ratio and reserve assumptions used in the projections in writing.
Have the Chief Financial Officer sign the projections before they are attached.
checklist.done: the plan of operation and three-year pro formas are actuarially supported and CFO-signed.

checklist.step: Clear the deposit, capital and surplus conditions the state attaches
actions: Read the state's statutory minimum capital and surplus for the requested lines and compare to the entity's latest quarterly statutory surplus.
Where the state requires a statutory deposit, arrange the securities deposit with the custodian and obtain the NAIC Form 6 certificate of deposit.
Confirm the deposit is registered on the NAIC Special Deposit Schedule so it is visible to every other state.
Attach the custodian confirmation and Form 6 to the case folder.
checklist.done: capital and surplus clear the state minimum and any required deposit is placed, certified on Form 6 and recorded on the deposit schedule.

checklist.step: Submit the application to the state and pay the filing fee
actions: Submit the pack through the state's stated channel — the state's UCAA instructions name either an electronic submission portal or a hard-copy address for the department's company licensing division.
Pay the Form 2 filing fee by the method the state accepts (EFT or check) and attach the payment confirmation to the case.
Record the submission date, the department contact name and the state's stated review period on the case.
Diary the follow-up date at submission date plus 30 days if no acknowledgement is received.
checklist.done: the application is submitted, the fee is paid and evidenced, and the submission date plus review period is on the case.

checklist.step: Work the state's objections until the CoA is granted
actions: Log each department objection letter on the case with its date and the response deadline the department set.
Assign each objection to the owning function — Treasury for deposits, Actuarial for reserve questions, Corporate Secretary for affidavit gaps — with a due date inside the department's deadline.
Send consolidated responses, never piecemeal, and keep the department contact copied on scheduling changes.
Where the state's grant will land after the target first-write date, tell the Insurance Product Manager and the Head of Distribution in writing the same week.
checklist.done: every objection is logged, owned and answered inside the department's deadline, and any slippage past the target date is communicated in writing.

checklist.step: Load the granted CoA into the corporate licensing register
actions: Attach the granted CoA certificate PDF to the register row and type the granted line codes exactly as printed on the certificate.
Record CoA number, grant date, effective date, any conditions or restrictions the department imposed, and the annual continuation date.
Set the register row status to ACTIVE and record the reviewer who compared the typed lines to the certificate.
Never load a line the certificate does not literally name.
checklist.done: the register row shows CoA number, granted lines transcribed from the certificate, effective date, conditions and continuation date, with the certificate attached.

checklist.step: Arm the state/line gate in the underwriting and quoting path
actions: Publish the register's active state/line grid to the underwriting workstation's eligibility table with the CoA effective date on each row.
Configure the quote path to refuse a risk whose state and statutory line pair is absent from the grid, with a message naming the missing CoA.
Run a test quote in the newly granted state before the effective date (must refuse) and after it (must allow), and screenshot both.
Give the underwriting team the earliest-bind date per state in writing.
checklist.done: the quoting path refuses out-of-CoA state/line pairs, proven by dated before-and-after test quotes.

checklist.step: Gate policy issuance and endorsement in the policy administration system
actions: Load the same state/line/effective-date grid into the issuance validation rules so a policy cannot be issued outside an active CoA line.
Extend the rule to mid-term endorsements that add a coverage in a different statutory line.
Date-effect the rule so back-dated policies are validated against the CoA as it stood on the policy effective date, not today.
Confirm the rule fires in the pre-production environment and record the release id.
checklist.done: issuance and endorsement validation blocks out-of-CoA lines using the CoA position as at the policy effective date, released under a recorded id.

checklist.step: Set the continuation, amendment and withdrawal triggers and file the evidence
actions: Diary each state's CoA continuation or annual renewal date with a 30-day reminder to the Regulatory Affairs Manager.
Register the corporate-change triggers that force an amendment filing: name change, redomestication, merger, change of control, officer or director change.
Move the case folder — checklist capture, submitted pack, objection correspondence, granted certificate, deposit evidence — into the evidence repository under Licensing / Corporate / <state>.
Apply the life-of-CoA plus 7-years retention label and confirm the record is searchable by writing company, state and CoA number.
checklist.done: continuation and amendment triggers are diarised and the full case folder is retained, labelled and retrievable by company, state and CoA number.

testing.step: Build the population of state/line pairs actually written in the quarter
actions: Extract every policy and endorsement with an effective date inside the quarter, carrying writing company, NAIC co-code, risk state and statutory annual statement line.
Reduce to distinct writing company x state x statutory line pairs and count the policies and written premium behind each pair.
Include surplus lines and assumed business separately so they are not silently netted out of the population.
Reconcile total written premium on the extract to the quarter's statutory premium by state before sampling and resolve any variance.
testing.done: the distinct-pair population reconciles to statutory written premium by state and is signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile every written pair to an active CoA in the licensing register
actions: Extract the licensing register: writing company, state, granted line codes, CoA effective date, status, conditions.
Left-join the written-pair population to the register on company plus state plus line and list every pair with no matching active row.
Check the register CoA effective date is on or before the earliest policy effective date in each pair.
Treat any unmatched pair, and any pair where the CoA post-dates the earliest policy, as an automatic exception with the premium quantified.
testing.done: every written pair is matched to a CoA effective on or before its earliest policy, or listed as a quantified exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of state/line pairs first written in the quarter and 100% of pairs in states entered in the last 12 months.
Take 20 further pairs at random from the remaining population using a recorded seed, for a minimum of 35 pairs.
Record population size, seed, selection date and selector in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Hand the sample list to the Regulatory Affairs Manager only after it is fixed, so it cannot be reshaped.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all newly entered pairs is fixed and recorded with its seed and population size.

testing.step: Re-perform the CoA verification against the certificate and the NAIC record
actions: For each sampled pair open the granted CoA certificate PDF and read the granted line list off the certificate itself.
Independently pull the NAIC jurisdiction/lines page for the writing company and compare it to both the certificate and the register.
Reach your own admitted / not-admitted conclusion for the line before reading the register status field.
Any three-way disagreement between certificate, NAIC record and register is an exception, including 'admitted but register line code wrong'.
testing.done: each sampled pair carries an independent admitted/not-admitted conclusion supported by the certificate and the NAIC jurisdiction page.

testing.step: Re-perform the statutory line mapping on the sampled products
actions: For each sampled pair take the actual policy form and coverage schedule, not the product summary.
Map the granted coverages to statutory annual statement lines yourself and compare to the mapping on the licensing case.
Pay particular attention to bundled products that reach into a second statutory line the CoA may not cover.
Flag every mapping difference — a wrong line mapping is how a company writes outside its CoA while believing it is inside.
testing.done: the auditor's own line mapping agrees with the licensing case for every sampled pair, or the difference is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Recompute the earliest-write date against the CoA effective date
actions: For each sampled pair pull the earliest policy effective date and the earliest bind/issue timestamp from the policy administration system.
Compare both to the CoA effective date printed on the certificate and record the day difference.
Check back-dated policies separately: a policy issued today but effective before the CoA date is a breach even though the issue date is clean.
Any negative day difference is a reportable unauthorised-business breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: every sampled pair shows a non-negative day difference between CoA effective date and earliest policy effective date, or the breach is quantified.

testing.step: Test that the system gate actually blocks an out-of-CoA state and line
actions: Pick three state/line pairs the register shows as not granted and attempt a quote and an issue in the test environment for each.
Confirm the attempt is refused with a message naming the missing CoA rather than merely warning the user.
Repeat one attempt with a back-dated effective date preceding a granted CoA to prove the rule is date-effective.
Screenshot each refusal with its timestamp into the workpaper.
testing.done: all three out-of-CoA attempts and the back-dated attempt are refused, evidenced by timestamped screenshots.

testing.step: Test the handling of conditions, amendments and withdrawals
actions: List every CoA in the register carrying a condition or restriction and read the condition text on the certificate.
For each, confirm the operating restriction is actually implemented — for example a line written only through a named managing agency, or a premium volume cap.
Check every corporate change in the period (name change, officer change, control change) has a matching amendment filing on the case log.
Check any state exited in the period has a filed withdrawal and that no new business was written after the withdrawal date.
testing.done: every CoA condition is implemented in operations and every corporate change or exit has a matching amendment or withdrawal filing.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception carrying writing company, state, statutory line, policy count and written premium exposed.
Assign a root cause from the standing list: line mapping error, register not updated from certificate, gate not date-effective, market entry launched ahead of grant.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and for any unauthorised-business breach open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel within 5 business days.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue with quantified premium exposure, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate over distinct written pairs and compare it to the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind each statement.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside Licensing & Appointments and prepared none of the sampled applications, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any unauthorised-business breach to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

checklist.step: Take in the producer candidate and open a licensing case
actions: Pull the new-producer request from the Agency Relations Manager carrying legal name, date of birth, resident state, National Producer Number (NPN) if held, and the states and products the producer will sell.
Create the producer record with Status = 'Verification pending' and no commission or quoting entitlement.
Where no NPN is supplied, search the producer by name and resident state in the NIPR Producer Database to find it before going further.
Reject the request back to Agency Relations if the state and product list is blank — the licence check cannot be scoped without it.
checklist.done: a producer record exists with NPN, resident state and the intended state/product list, held in 'Verification pending' with no entitlements.

checklist.step: Pull the NIPR Producer Database report and file it dated
actions: Sign in to NIPR with the company account and open the Producer Database (PDB) report by NPN.
Print the full PDB report to PDF including the licence summary, the lines of authority per state, the appointment section and the regulatory actions section.
Name the file <NPN>-pdb-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf and attach it to the producer record — this dated capture is the evidence behind the verification.
Never verify from a screenshot of a single line; the LOA and action sections both drive the decision.
checklist.done: a complete dated PDB report PDF is attached to the producer record.

checklist.step: Match licence class and lines of authority to the products the producer will sell
actions: For each intended state, read the licence class (Producer, Business Entity, Limited Lines) and the granted lines of authority (Property, Casualty, Personal Lines, Life, Accident & Health, Variable).
Map each product the producer will sell to the LOA it requires and tick it off state by state on the verification worksheet.
Where a product needs an LOA the producer lacks, block that product for that state and tell the Agency Relations Manager in writing which combinations are unavailable.
Record variable products separately — they additionally need FINRA registration, which the PDB does not evidence.
checklist.done: every intended state/product combination is ticked to a granted LOA or explicitly blocked, on a saved worksheet.

checklist.step: Check licence status, effective and expiration dates in every intended state
actions: For each state on the PDB read Status (Active, Inactive, Expired, Suspended, Revoked), the licence issue date and the expiration date.
Reject any state showing anything other than Active and record the reason on the worksheet.
Flag any state whose expiration date falls within 90 days so the renewal track picks the producer up immediately.
Where the PDB conflicts with the state department's own licence lookup, treat the state lookup as authoritative and note the conflict.
checklist.done: each intended state shows an Active licence with dates recorded, and near-expiry states are handed to the renewal track.

checklist.step: Review regulatory actions and administrative history before clearing the producer
actions: Read the PDB regulatory actions section, which surfaces Regulatory Information Retrieval System (RIRS) entries, and the Special Activities Database entries where present.
For every action recorded, obtain the state's order or consent decree and read the conduct behind it, not the summary code.
Escalate any action involving misappropriation of premium, forgery, unlicensed activity or a felony to Regulatory Counsel before contracting proceeds.
Record the decision — clear, clear with conditions, or decline — with the reviewer name and date on the producer record.
checklist.done: every RIRS/SAD entry is read at source and the producer carries a dated clear, clear-with-conditions or decline decision.

checklist.step: File the non-resident licence application where a needed state licence is missing
actions: Confirm the producer holds an active resident licence with the LOA required — non-resident licensure is reciprocal off the home state licence under Model 218 section 9.
In NIPR open Non-Resident Licensing, select the target state, and complete the application with the producer's NPN, LOA requested and background questions.
Pay the state licence fee plus the NIPR transaction fee from the funded company account and capture the transaction confirmation number.
Diary the application at submission plus 10 business days and chase the state through its own licensing division if no issuance appears on the PDB.
checklist.done: each missing state licence has a submitted NIPR non-resident application with a confirmation number and a chase diary date.

checklist.step: Hold the solicitation block until verification is complete
actions: Keep the producer's CRM record flagged 'Not authorised to solicit' so no lead, campaign or quote can be assigned to them.
Confirm the marketing automation suppression list excludes unverified producers from co-branded campaign material.
Give Agency Relations a written statement of what the producer may and may not do while pending — no solicitation, no quoting, no application taking.
Release the flag only on the Producer Licensing Coordinator's dated verification, never on a verbal assurance.
checklist.done: the producer cannot be assigned leads, quotes or campaigns until a dated verification releases the flag.

checklist.step: Verify once more immediately before submitting the appointment
actions: Re-pull the PDB report on the day the appointment transaction will be submitted — licences lapse between onboarding and appointment.
Confirm the state still shows Active with the LOA the appointment will carry.
Attach the second dated PDB capture to the appointment request as the pre-appointment evidence.
Abandon the appointment transaction and return the case to licensing if the status has moved.
checklist.done: a same-day PDB capture showing an Active licence with the matching LOA is attached to every appointment request.

checklist.step: Handle agency licensing and the designated responsible licensed producer
actions: For every agency the company contracts with, pull the business entity PDB record and confirm the entity licence is Active in each state where its producers will write.
Confirm a Designated Responsible Licensed Producer (DRLP) is named for each state that requires one, and that the named individual's own licence is Active with matching LOA.
Record the entity FEIN, entity NPN and DRLP NPN on the agency record.
Diary DRLP changes as a licensing event — a DRLP departure can invalidate the entity licence in that state.
checklist.done: each contracted agency has an Active entity licence per state with a named, licensed DRLP recorded against the agency record.

checklist.step: Release contracting only after verification clears
actions: Check the producer record shows Verification = Cleared with a dated PDB attachment before issuing the producer agreement.
Issue the producer agreement and commission schedule for signature, restricting the schedule to the states and LOAs verified.
Capture the executed agreement date — under Model 218 section 13 this date starts the appointment filing clock in most states.
File the executed agreement against the producer record and notify Licensing Ops of the execution date the same day.
checklist.done: the executed producer agreement is on file, limited to verified states and LOAs, with its execution date notified to Licensing Ops.

checklist.step: Write the verified state/LOA grid back into the producer master
actions: Load the verified rows — NPN, state, licence class, LOA, status, expiration date, verification date — into the producer master as the single source for downstream gates.
Set the record's authorised-to-sell grid from those rows rather than from the contract, so a lapse removes authorisation automatically.
Run a duplicate check on NPN and FEIN to prevent two records for the same producer holding different states.
Log the load with a record count and reconcile it to the number of verified rows.
checklist.done: the producer master holds one deduplicated record per NPN whose authorised-to-sell grid derives from verified licence rows.

checklist.step: Gate application intake and binding on the writing producer's licence
actions: Configure new business intake to require a writing producer NPN on every application and to validate it against the producer master grid for the risk state and product LOA.
Make the validation date-effective against the application signature date, not the entry date, so back-dated applications are tested correctly.
Refuse the bind with a message naming the missing state or LOA rather than warning and continuing.
Test one refusal and one pass in pre-production and record the release id.
checklist.done: binding is refused when the writing producer lacks an active licence and LOA for the risk state as at the application signature date.

checklist.step: Certify the producer on the products before first sale
actions: Assign the product training and any state-mandated training the LOA requires — annuity suitability training and long-term care training are common prerequisites to selling those products.
Record completion dates and course provider against the producer record.
Block the specific product, not the producer, where a state-mandated course is outstanding.
Give Licensing Ops a monthly list of producers selling a product whose mandatory training is incomplete.
checklist.done: no producer can sell a product whose state-mandated training is incomplete, with completion dates recorded per producer.

checklist.step: Run continuous licence status monitoring, not a one-off check
actions: Subscribe the company's NPN list to the NIPR alert/status service so licence status changes arrive without a manual pull.
Load the daily change file into the producer master and auto-suspend the authorised-to-sell grid for any producer moving to Expired, Inactive, Suspended or Revoked.
Route every suspension to the Agency Relations Manager the same day with the affected states and the in-flight applications involved.
Reconcile the change file record count to the alerts processed each day and investigate any shortfall.
checklist.done: licence status changes are ingested daily, authorisation is auto-suspended on adverse status, and the file is reconciled to alerts processed.

checklist.step: Retain the verification evidence for the required period
actions: Move the dated PDB captures, LOA match worksheet, RIRS review note and contracting approval into the evidence repository under Licensing / Producer / <NPN>.
Apply the relationship-plus-5-years retention label so records survive the producer's departure.
Restrict access to Licensing, Compliance and Audit — the file carries personal and regulatory action data.
Confirm the record is retrievable by NPN, producer name, state and verification date.
checklist.done: the verification file is retained under the relationship-plus-5-years label, access-restricted and retrievable by NPN and state.

testing.step: Build the population of producers who transacted in the quarter
actions: Extract every application submitted and policy bound in the quarter with writing producer NPN, agency NPN, risk state, product, application signature date and bind date.
Add commission payments made in the quarter from the commission platform so producers paid but not showing as writing agents are caught.
Reduce to distinct producer x state x LOA-required combinations and count the business behind each.
Reconcile the extract's policy count and premium to the quarter's new business report before sampling.
testing.done: the producer x state x LOA population reconciles to the new business report and to commission payees, signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the producer master and to the PDB
actions: Join the population to the producer master on NPN and list every transacting NPN with no producer master record.
For matched rows, compare the master's authorised state/LOA grid to the LOA the transacted product required.
Pull a fresh bulk PDB extract for every NPN in the population and compare licence status and LOA to the master.
Treat any master-versus-PDB disagreement as an automatic exception — the master is meant to be derived from the PDB.
testing.done: every transacting NPN is matched to a master record whose state/LOA grid agrees with a freshly pulled PDB extract, or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of producers onboarded in the quarter and 100% of producers with any RIRS entry on the PDB.
Take 25 further producer/state rows at random from the remaining population using a recorded seed, minimum 45 rows overall.
Record population size, seed, selection date and selector so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Fix the sample before notifying Licensing Ops.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all new and RIRS-flagged producers is fixed and documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the PDB licence verification for each sampled row
actions: Open the NIPR Producer Database report for the sampled NPN and read the state's licence status, class, LOA, issue date and expiration date yourself.
Reach an independent licensed / not-licensed conclusion for that state and LOA before opening the licensing case file.
Compare to the recorded verification; a right conclusion supported by the wrong LOA is still an exception.
Print the PDB page relied on into the workpaper with its retrieval timestamp.
testing.done: each sampled row has an independent PDB re-performance note and a timestamped source capture.

testing.step: Test that the licence was active on the solicitation date, not merely today
actions: For each sampled row take the earliest application signature date attributed to that producer in that state.
Compare it to the licence issue date on the PDB and compute the day difference.
Where the licence issue date is later than the application signature date, quantify the policies and premium solicited unlicensed.
Check for licences that lapsed and were reinstated mid-quarter — business written in the gap is a breach even though the licence now shows Active.
testing.done: every sampled row shows the licence issued on or before the earliest application signature date, or the unlicensed business is quantified.

testing.step: Test the line-of-authority match against what was actually sold
actions: For each sampled row list the products actually sold from the policy extract, not the products the producer was approved for.
Map each product to the LOA it requires under that state's licensing rules and compare to the granted LOA on the PDB.
Give particular attention to variable and annuity products, which need Life plus Variable LOA and, for variable, FINRA registration.
Log any product sold outside the granted LOA with the policy count and the consumers affected.
testing.done: every product sold in the sample maps to a granted LOA, or the out-of-LOA sales are logged with consumer counts.

testing.step: Test agency entity licensing and DRLP coverage in the sample
actions: For every agency appearing in the sample pull the business entity PDB record and confirm the entity licence is Active in the state of the business.
Confirm the named DRLP on the agency record matches the DRLP shown on the state record and that the DRLP's own licence is Active.
Check DRLP changes during the quarter were reflected with the state, since a stale DRLP can void the entity licence.
Log any agency writing on an inactive entity licence with the premium involved.
testing.done: every sampled agency holds an Active entity licence with a matching, licensed DRLP, or the gap is logged with premium.

testing.step: Test the intake gate and the continuous monitoring feed
actions: Attempt to bind three test applications naming producers who are unlicensed in the risk state and confirm each is refused with the state/LOA named.
Attempt one back-dated application whose signature date precedes the producer's licence issue date and confirm it is refused.
Take one day's NIPR status change file and trace each adverse status change through to an authorisation suspension in the producer master within one business day.
Screenshot each refusal and the traced suspension into the workpaper.
testing.done: all four blocked attempts are refused and every adverse status change on the tested day suspended authorisation within one business day.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying NPN, producer name, state, LOA, policies affected, premium and commission paid.
Assign a root cause from the standing list: verification skipped, LOA mis-mapped, master not refreshed from PDB, gate not date-effective, status change not ingested.
Set an owner and remediation date, including the commission clawback decision where business was solicited unlicensed.
Carry every open exception into the next monthly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue with quantified policies, premium and commission, plus root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate over transacting producer/state rows and compare it to the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper reference for each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside Licensing Ops and performed none of the sampled verifications, sign the workpaper.
Report unlicensed-solicitation findings to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

checklist.step: Capture the appointment trigger event and start the statutory clock
actions: Take the two feeds that can start the clock: executed producer agreements from Contract Administration and first-application-submitted events from the new business intake.
Set the trigger date to the earlier of the contract execution date and the first application submission date, per Model 218 section 13.
Create an appointment task per producer per state with the trigger date and the computed statutory due date visible on the task.
Reject any feed row with a blank trigger date back to the source system the same day — a blank date silently disarms the clock.
checklist.done: each appointment task shows the earlier of contract execution and first application as its trigger date, with no blank dates in the feed.

checklist.step: Compute the state-specific due date rather than assuming 15 days
actions: Open the state appointment rules table and read that state's appointment filing window, whether it counts calendar or business days, and whether it runs from contract execution or first application only.
Record the window and the counting basis on the task alongside the computed due date.
Re-read the source statute annually and on any department bulletin, updating the rules table with the effective date of the change.
Flag the states that do not require individual appointments at all so the queue does not generate needless transactions.
checklist.done: each task carries a due date computed from that state's own window and counting basis, sourced from a dated rules table.

checklist.step: Re-verify the licence immediately before filing the appointment
actions: Pull a same-day Producer Database report for the NPN and confirm the state licence is Active with the LOA the appointment will carry.
Confirm the licence expiration date is more than 30 days away, or route the producer to the renewal track first.
Attach the same-day PDB capture to the appointment task.
Hold the transaction and notify the Agency Relations Manager if the status has moved since onboarding — a rejected appointment burns clock days.
checklist.done: every appointment task carries a same-day PDB capture showing an Active licence with matching LOA before submission.

checklist.step: Build the NIPR appointment transaction batch
actions: In NIPR Gateway open Appointments and start a new appointment transaction for the company FEIN and NAIC co-code.
Enter per row: producer NPN, state, appointment type (individual or business entity), lines of authority to appoint and requested appointment effective date.
Where the state requires an appointing agency hierarchy, enter the agency NPN the producer appoints under.
Validate the batch against the file layout before submission and correct format rejects offline rather than resubmitting blind.
checklist.done: a validated appointment batch is staged with NPN, state, type, LOA and effective date on every row.

checklist.step: Fund the account and confirm the state appointment fee
actions: Check the NIPR company account balance against the batch's total state appointment fees plus NIPR transaction fees before submission.
Top up the account where the balance will not cover the batch — an underfunded account rejects the whole batch and consumes clock days.
Reconcile the NIPR account statement to the general ledger appointment fee account monthly.
Flag states whose fee has changed so the rules table and the budget are updated.
checklist.done: the NIPR account covers the batch before submission and the account statement reconciles to the ledger monthly.

checklist.step: Submit the batch and capture the transaction confirmations
actions: Submit the appointment batch and download the transaction response file the same day.
Record the NIPR transaction confirmation number, submission timestamp and state-assigned appointment effective date against each producer/state task.
Close only the rows the response confirms as accepted; leave rejected rows open on the original clock.
Attach the response file to the batch record as filing evidence.
checklist.done: every accepted row carries a confirmation number, submission timestamp and appointment effective date; rejects stay open on the original clock.

checklist.step: Work rejects inside the remaining clock days
actions: Triage each reject reason: licence not active, LOA not held, duplicate appointment already on file, fee shortfall, entity not licensed in state.
Fix and resubmit within 2 business days, and record the reject reason and fix on the task so root causes are visible.
Escalate to the Producer Compliance Manager any reject that cannot be cured before the statutory due date.
Never close a rejected row by marking the appointment as not required without a rules-table citation.
checklist.done: every reject is triaged, cured within 2 business days or escalated before the due date, with the reason recorded.

checklist.step: Release commissions and new business only on a confirmed appointment
actions: Set the commission schedule to pay only where an appointment effective date exists for the producer, state and LOA of the policy.
Hold commission on business written before the appointment effective date and route it to the Producer Compliance Manager for a written decision.
Feed the appointment effective dates into the commission engine daily from the producer master, not by manual entry.
Report held commission by producer and state monthly to the Head of Distribution.
checklist.done: commission pays only against a confirmed appointment for the policy's state and LOA, with holds reported monthly.

checklist.step: Capture the termination trigger with a cause code
actions: Take termination events from three sources: HR leaver feed for employed producers, contract termination notices for independent producers, and agency-initiated departures reported by the agency.

Record the termination effective date and a cause code — resignation, non-production, restructuring, or a conduct reason such as premium misappropriation, forgery, misrepresentation or unlicensed activity.
Attach the underlying evidence for any conduct code: investigation report, customer complaint, audit finding.
Send every conduct-coded termination to the Producer Compliance Manager the same day.
checklist.done: every termination carries an effective date, a cause code and, for conduct codes, attached evidence routed to Compliance the same day.

checklist.step: Determine whether the termination must be reported for cause
actions: Read Model 218 section 14 as adopted in each affected state and identify the reportable causes — the section 12 grounds, including fraud, misappropriation, forgery and licence violations.
Read the investigation file and decide, in writing, whether the facts meet the reportable-cause standard in each state.
Where cause is reportable, list the supporting documents the state expects and confirm the statutory immunity conditions are satisfied.
Record the decision, the reasoning and the date on the termination record; a decision not to report cause is documented with the same rigour.
checklist.done: a dated written counsel determination exists on cause reportability for every conduct-coded termination, in each affected state.

checklist.step: File the termination in NIPR within the statutory window
actions: In NIPR Gateway open Terminations and enter producer NPN, state, termination effective date and the termination reason code the state requires.
For for-cause terminations select the cause reason and upload the supporting documents through the NIPR Attachments Warehouse where the state accepts it.
Submit within 30 days of the termination effective date and record the confirmation number and submission timestamp.
File the supplemental information a state requests within 30 days of the company discovering it, as a further transaction on the same producer/state.
checklist.done: every termination is filed within 30 days of its effective date with a captured confirmation number, and for-cause documents are uploaded.

checklist.step: Send the producer their copy of the termination notice
actions: Generate the producer notice reproducing the notification made to the state, including the reason reported.
Send it to the producer's last known address of record within 15 days of the state filing, using a method that evidences dispatch.
Record the dispatch date and method on the termination record and file the signed notice copy.
Log and route to Regulatory Counsel any producer response disputing the reported cause, since the state must receive the additional information.
checklist.done: the producer notice is dispatched within 15 days of the state filing with dispatch date and method recorded, and disputes are routed to counsel.

checklist.step: Shut off access, quoting and new business on the termination date
actions: Disable the producer's portal and quoting access effective on the termination date, not on the filing date.
Reassign in-flight quotes and pending applications to a licensed, appointed producer and tell the affected customers who now services them.
Set the book of business servicing arrangement and confirm renewal notices will not name the terminated producer.
Confirm the shut-off with a screenshot of the disabled account and file it against the termination record.
checklist.done: access is disabled on the termination effective date and every in-flight item is reassigned to a licensed, appointed producer.

checklist.step: Escalate and remediate any missed window immediately
actions: Run the open-task ageing daily and identify any appointment past day 15 or termination past day 30 from its trigger date.
File the late transaction the same day it is identified rather than waiting for a batch cycle.
Raise a tracker issue with the state, NPN, trigger date, filing date, day count and any state late fee or penalty.
Where a state requires a written explanation of a late appointment, draft it with Regulatory Counsel before submission.
checklist.done: no task ages past its statutory window undetected, and every late filing has a same-day submission and a tracker issue with the day count.

checklist.step: Retain appointment and termination evidence for the full period
actions: Move confirmation numbers, response files, for-cause files, counsel determinations and producer notices into the evidence repository under Licensing / Appointments / <state> / <NPN>.
Apply a 7-years-from-termination retention label and restrict for-cause files to Compliance, Legal and Audit.
Confirm the record is retrievable by NPN, state, transaction confirmation number and effective date.
Reconcile the repository record count to the NIPR transaction count for the month.
checklist.done: every transaction is retained under a 7-year label, access-restricted where for-cause, and the repository count reconciles to NIPR transactions.

testing.step: Build the population of appointment and termination events for the month
actions: Extract every executed producer agreement, every first-application-submitted event and every termination event with a trigger date in the month.
Pull the HR leaver feed and the contract termination notices independently and add any event missing from the licensing queue.
Build the population as producer x state x event type with trigger date, cause code and current status.
Reconcile the event count to the source systems and resolve every difference before sampling.
testing.done: the event population reconciles to contract, new business and HR sources and is signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile every event to a NIPR transaction
actions: Download the company's NIPR appointment and termination transaction history for the month and the following month.
Match each population event to a transaction on NPN plus state plus event type.
List every event with no matching transaction, and every transaction with no matching internal event, as automatic exceptions.
Investigate orphan transactions specifically — an appointment filed with no contract behind it points at a control gap in contracting.
testing.done: every event matches a NIPR transaction and every transaction matches an internal event, or the orphan is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of for-cause terminations and 100% of events in states with windows shorter than the 15-day model default.
Take 30 further events at random from the remaining population using a recorded seed, minimum 50 events overall.
Record population size, seed, selection date and selector in the workpaper.
Fix the sample before Licensing Ops sees it.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all for-cause terminations and short-window states is fixed and documented.

testing.step: Recompute the statutory day count for each sampled event
actions: Take the trigger date from the source record — the executed agreement or the application signature, whichever is earlier — not from the licensing task.
Read the state's own window and counting basis from the statute rather than the internal rules table.
Recompute days elapsed from trigger date to NIPR submission timestamp and compare to the window.
Any recomputed count exceeding the window is a fail, including counts the internal task shows as within window because it used the later trigger date.
testing.done: each sampled event has an independently recomputed day count measured from the source trigger date against the statute's own window.

testing.step: Re-perform the trigger-date determination on the sampled appointments
actions: For each sampled appointment pull every application in that state attributed to the producer and identify the earliest application signature date.
Compare it to the executed agreement date and determine the earlier of the two yourself.
Compare your trigger date to the one the licensing task used and log any difference with the days it shifts the due date.
Look specifically for applications taken before contracting — a common source of an under-stated clock.
testing.done: the auditor's own earlier-of trigger date agrees with the licensing task for every sampled appointment, or the shift is logged.

testing.step: Trace each sampled filing to its NIPR confirmation and state record
actions: Search the recorded NIPR transaction confirmation number and open the transaction detail.
Confirm it names the right company FEIN, producer NPN, state, LOA and effective date.
Pull the producer's current PDB report and confirm the appointment or termination now shows in the appointment section with the expected effective date.
Capture both the transaction detail and the PDB appointment section into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled filing traces to a NIPR confirmation whose details match, and the outcome is visible on the producer's PDB record.

testing.step: Test the for-cause determinations and the producer notice
actions: For every for-cause termination in the sample read the investigation file and reach an independent view on whether the facts meet the state's reportable-cause standard.
Confirm the cause reason reported to the state matches the counsel determination and the underlying evidence.
Confirm the producer notice reproduces what was reported and was dispatched within 15 days of the state filing, with dispatch evidence.
Treat a conduct-coded termination reported as a plain termination as a reportable breach, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every for-cause termination is supported by an independent counsel view, a matching state report and a dated producer notice within 15 days.

testing.step: Test that no business was written or commission paid outside the appointment
actions: For each sampled producer/state pull the policies bound and commissions paid, with dates, for the quarter.
Compare each bind date to the appointment effective date and each commission payment to the appointment and termination window.
List business bound before the appointment effective date and commission paid after a termination effective date, with amounts.
Check that renewal commission arrangements after termination follow the contract and the state's rules rather than defaulting on.
testing.done: no sampled policy was bound before its appointment effective date and no commission was paid outside the appointment window, or amounts are quantified.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying NPN, state, event type, trigger date, filing date, recomputed day count and any state penalty.
Assign a root cause from the standing list: trigger feed missing, wrong counting basis, NIPR reject not worked, account underfunded, for-cause misclassified.
Set an owner and remediation date, and for missed windows record whether the state was told and by whom.
Carry every open exception into the next month's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue with the recomputed day count, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the on-time filing rate for appointments and for terminations separately and compare each to the zero-missed-window threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper reference behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who submitted none of the sampled NIPR transactions, sign the workpaper.
Report missed windows and for-cause findings to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with separate appointment and termination timeliness rates, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed.
