checklist.step: Build the rolling renewal calendar from licence expiration dates
actions: Pull the bulk Producer Database extract for every appointed NPN and take the expiration date, licence class and LOA per state.
Load the extract into the renewal calendar keyed on NPN plus state, refreshing at least weekly so newly issued licences appear.
Separate resident licences, which drive the CE obligation, from non-resident licences, which usually renew on home-state CE.
Reconcile the calendar row count to the appointed producer count per state and investigate any producer with an appointment but no licence row.
checklist.done: the calendar holds a dated expiration row per NPN per state, refreshed weekly and reconciled to the appointed producer count.

checklist.step: Record each state's own renewal cycle and CE requirement
actions: For every state maintain the rules table row: renewal frequency (usually biennial), the anchor (birth month, licence anniversary or fixed date), total CE hours, ethics hours, and any product-specific hours such as annuity or long-term care.
Record whether the state requires CE to be completed and reported before the renewal submission or merely before the expiry date.
Record the grace or reinstatement window and the penalty fee, and whether the state permits transacting during the grace period (most do not).
Date every rules-table change with the bulletin or statute that drove it and re-verify all 51 rows annually.
checklist.done: each state has a dated rules-table row covering cycle anchor, CE hours, ethics hours, reporting rule and grace window.

checklist.step: Pull CE transcripts and compute credits against the requirement
actions: Run the CE transcript enquiry for each resident NPN and download the state-reported credit detail with course numbers, provider, credit hours and completion dates.
Compute credits earned inside the current compliance period only — credits from a prior cycle do not carry unless the state allows carry-forward.
Split the total into general hours and ethics hours and compare each separately to the state requirement.
Record the computed shortfall per producer per category on the renewal calendar row.
checklist.done: each resident producer row shows state-reported general and ethics credits for the current period and a computed shortfall per category.

checklist.step: Detect and publish shortfalls at 120 days to expiry
actions: Run the shortfall report 120 days before each expiry date, listing producer, state, hours short, ethics hours short and days remaining.
Send the list to the Agency Relations Manager and the producer's territory manager, not only to the producer.
Rank by exposure — producers with the largest in-force book first, because their lapse costs most.
Publish the report to the distribution leadership dashboard so shortfalls are visible outside Licensing.
checklist.done: a T-120 shortfall report by producer and state is published to distribution leadership with hours short and days remaining.

checklist.step: Assign state-approved courses to close the shortfall
actions: Match each shortfall to courses carrying that state's approved course number for the correct category, since a general course cannot fill an ethics shortfall.
Assign the courses with a completion due date at least 30 days before expiry to leave room for provider reporting lag.
Confirm the provider is approved in that state and reports credits to the state on the producer's behalf.
Record the assignment, the state course number and the due date against the producer's renewal row.
checklist.done: each shortfall has assigned courses with state-approved course numbers in the right category and a due date 30 days before expiry.

checklist.step: Track completions through to the state's own record
actions: Take weekly completion data from the LMS and mark the renewal row 'course completed, awaiting state posting'.
Re-run the CE transcript enquiry 10 days after each completion and confirm the credit has posted at the state.
Chase the provider directly where a credit has not posted within 15 days — an unposted credit is not a completed credit to the state.
Only mark a producer CE-compliant when the state transcript, not the LMS, shows the required hours.
checklist.done: CE compliance is marked only from the state transcript, with unposted credits chased with the provider within 15 days.

checklist.step: Notify producers on the escalating reminder schedule
actions: Send automated reminders at T-90, T-60, T-30 and T-10 days naming the state, the expiry date, the hours outstanding and the renewal fee.
Post the same status to the producer's portal dashboard so it is visible at every login.
Escalate T-30 non-responders to their territory manager with a request for a written commitment date.
Log every reminder sent with its timestamp so the notification trail is evidencable.
checklist.done: reminders are sent and logged at T-90/T-60/T-30/T-10 with hours outstanding, and T-30 non-responders are escalated to their territory manager.

checklist.step: Submit the licence renewal before the expiry date
actions: In NIPR open Licensing Renewal, select the state and NPN, and answer the background and disclosure questions from current data, not last cycle's answers.
Confirm the state's CE compliance flag shows satisfied before submitting, since many states reject a renewal on an open CE deficiency.
Pay the state renewal fee and the NIPR transaction fee and capture the confirmation number and submission timestamp.
Re-pull the PDB 5 business days later and confirm the new expiration date has posted.
checklist.done: the renewal is submitted before expiry with a captured confirmation number, and the new expiration date is confirmed on the PDB.

checklist.step: Handle the state appointment renewal billing cycle
actions: Take each state's appointment renewal invoice or NIPR electronic appointment renewal file on its published cycle date.
Reconcile the billed appointments to the active producer roster and mark for non-renewal any appointment for a producer who has left or is no longer writing.
Approve payment for the remainder and record the paid appointment list with the renewal effective dates.
Report the fee saved by cancelling stale appointments to the Head of Distribution each cycle.
checklist.done: each state's appointment renewal is reconciled to the active roster before payment, with stale appointments cancelled and savings reported.

checklist.step: Escalate producers still non-compliant at 15 days to expiry
actions: Run the T-15 list and call each producer and their territory manager personally rather than sending another email.
Agree either a completion plan that finishes inside the window or a controlled wind-down of their pipeline.
Warn in writing that the licence will lapse, appointments will be suspended and in-flight applications will be reassigned.
Record the conversation, the commitment and the owner on the renewal row.
checklist.done: every T-15 non-compliant producer has a recorded conversation with either a completion plan or a wind-down decision.

checklist.step: Suspend authorisation the moment a licence expires
actions: Take the daily NIPR status change file and set the authorised-to-sell grid to suspended for any state moving to Expired or Inactive.
Disable quoting and application entry for that producer in that state the same day, and stop commission on new business.
Reassign in-flight quotes and pending applications to a licensed, appointed producer and notify the affected customers.
Confirm whether the state also cancels the appointment on lapse and, if so, queue a new appointment for after reinstatement.
checklist.done: expired licences suspend authorisation and stop new business the same day, with in-flight work reassigned.

checklist.step: Work reinstatement inside the state's grace window
actions: Read the state's reinstatement rule from the rules table: window length, penalty fee, whether outstanding CE must be completed first, and whether re-examination is required after the window closes.
Complete the outstanding CE and confirm it has posted to the state transcript before submitting reinstatement.
Submit the reinstatement with the penalty fee and capture the confirmation number and the reinstated effective date.
Re-file the appointment where the state cancelled it on lapse, and record the new appointment effective date.
checklist.done: reinstatement is submitted inside the state window with CE posted, the penalty paid and any cancelled appointment re-filed.

checklist.step: Assess and remediate business written during any lapse
actions: Extract every application, bind and commission payment attributed to the producer between the expiry date and the reinstatement date.
Assess the state's position on business transacted without a licence and whether self-reporting or policyholder remediation is required.
Decide the commission treatment — most states prohibit paying commission for business transacted unlicensed.
Record the assessment, the decision and the notification made, if any, on the lapse record.
checklist.done: every lapse has a written counsel assessment of the business transacted in the gap, with a commission and self-report decision recorded.

checklist.step: Report renewal and CE performance to distribution leadership
actions: Publish a monthly dashboard: on-time renewal rate, licences lapsed, average days-to-reinstatement, CE shortfall count at T-120 and at T-30, appointment fee spend.
Break the numbers down by territory and agency so accountability sits with the relationship owner.
Include a named list of producers whose licences expire in the next 90 days with hours outstanding.
Table the dashboard at the monthly distribution operations meeting and minute the actions.
checklist.done: a monthly renewal and CE dashboard broken down by territory and agency is tabled and its actions are minuted.

checklist.step: Retain the renewal and CE evidence for the audit look-back
actions: Move renewal confirmations, state CE transcripts, course completion certificates and reminder logs into the evidence repository under Licensing / Renewals / <NPN>.
Apply a 5-years-from-renewal retention label to match the CE audit look-back states typically apply.
Confirm the record is retrievable by NPN, state, expiry date and compliance period.
Reconcile the repository record count to the renewals submitted in the period.
checklist.done: renewal and CE evidence is retained under a 5-year label, retrievable by NPN and period, with counts reconciled to renewals submitted.

testing.step: Build the population of licences expiring in the quarter
actions: Pull an independent bulk PDB extract for every appointed NPN and select rows with an expiration date inside the quarter.
Add every licence that actually moved to Expired during the quarter, whether or not it was on the internal calendar.
Build the population as NPN x state with expiry date, resident flag, licence class and LOA.
Reconcile the population count to the internal renewal calendar and treat any calendar gap as an immediate control finding.
testing.done: the expiring-licence population is built from an independent PDB extract and reconciled to the internal renewal calendar.

testing.step: Reconcile every expiring licence to a renewal outcome
actions: For each population row read the current PDB status and the current expiration date.
Classify each row as renewed on time, renewed after expiry, reinstated, lapsed and open, or terminated.
Compare the classification to the internal renewal log and list every disagreement.
Treat any licence renewed after expiry as a fail even where the state permitted a grace period.
testing.done: every expiring licence carries a PDB-derived outcome classification reconciled to the internal renewal log.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of licences that lapsed and 100% of resident licences whose CE compliance date fell in the quarter.
Take 25 further rows at random from the remaining population using a recorded seed, minimum 40 rows overall.
Record population size, seed, selection date and selector so the sample can be re-drawn.
Fix the sample before requesting the licensing files.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering every lapse and every in-period CE compliance date is fixed and documented.

testing.step: Recompute CE credits independently from the state transcript
actions: Pull the state CE transcript for each sampled resident NPN yourself and list every posted course with hours, category and completion date.
Recompute general hours and ethics hours earned inside the compliance period, excluding courses completed outside it and duplicate course numbers the state will not double count.
Compare your totals to the state requirement in the rules table and to the licensing team's computed figure.
Any difference in either category is an exception, including a right total built from a wrong category split.
testing.done: each sampled producer has independently recomputed general and ethics hours agreeing to the requirement, or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Verify the state rules table against the state's own published requirement
actions: Take 10 states from the sample and read each state department's current producer CE and renewal page directly.
Compare cycle anchor, total hours, ethics hours, product-specific hours, grace window and penalty to the internal rules table row.
Log any stale row with the date the state changed it and the producers affected in the interim.
Treat a stale rules-table row as a systemic exception, since it mis-states the obligation for every producer in that state.
testing.done: 10 states are re-verified against the department's own published requirement and every stale rules-table row is logged as systemic.

testing.step: Recompute the renewal timing and the reminder trail
actions: For each sampled row compute days between the renewal submission timestamp and the expiration date.
Confirm the reminder log holds sent-timestamps at T-90, T-60, T-30 and T-10, and that the T-120 shortfall report listed the producer where a shortfall existed.
Log rows renewed inside 10 days of expiry as a timeliness concern even where they passed, since they carry no room for provider reporting lag.
Log any row with no reminder trail as a control failure independent of the renewal outcome.
testing.done: every sampled row has a recomputed renewal lead time and a complete evidenced reminder trail, or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Test for business transacted on a lapsed licence
actions: For every lapsed licence in the population extract applications signed, policies bound and endorsements issued between the expiry date and the reinstatement or termination date.
Quantify policy count, premium and commission paid in the lapse window by state.
Confirm the authorised-to-sell suspension actually fired on the expiry date by reading the producer master change history.
Any transaction inside the lapse window is a reportable breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: every lapse window is swept for transactions, with policy count, premium and commission quantified and the suspension timing verified.

testing.step: Test the appointment renewal reconciliation for stale appointments
actions: Take the quarter's state appointment renewal invoices and match every billed appointment to an active producer on the roster.
List appointments renewed for producers terminated before the billing date and quantify the fees wasted.
Confirm the cancellation instruction for each stale appointment was submitted before the state's non-renewal cut-off.
Check that no producer was left appointed but unlicensed after the renewal cycle.
testing.done: every billed appointment ties to an active producer, stale appointments were cancelled before cut-off, and no appointed-but-unlicensed producer remains.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying NPN, state, expiry date, renewal date, CE hours short and any business written during a lapse.
Assign a root cause from the standing list: calendar not refreshed, CE credits not posted at state, wrong category split, producer non-responsive, stale rules-table row.
Set an owner and remediation date, and for lapse-window business record the counsel assessment reference.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue with the CE and timing detail, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the on-time renewal rate and the CE compliance rate and compare each to the 100% target.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper reference behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who processed none of the sampled renewals, sign the workpaper.
Report lapses and any lapse-window business to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with the on-time renewal rate, CE compliance rate, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the 18 U.S.C. 1033 screening and adjudication gate for every producer and insurance-function hire; escalation to Regulatory Counsel on any felony involving dishonesty or breach of trust

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 18 U.S.C. 1033(e) (prohibited persons and the 1033(e)(2) written consent) and 1034 (civil enforcement), plus NAIC Model 218 section 12 licence denial grounds and each state's own background and fingerprint requirement (rep: Alabama Ala. Code Title 27 Chapter 7; supporting: Arizona, California, Connecticut)

In-scope processes.value: Producer contracting and employee hiring into any role that transacts the business of insurance: consent capture, criminal background check, fingerprinting where the state requires it, regulatory action search, adjudication and 1033 consent tracking

In-scope systems.value: Background screening and criminal records search, supported by NIPR PDB regulatory action data and the HRIS applicant record; adjudication outcome written to the producer master and the HRIS

Compliance procedure documented.value: 1033 Screening & Adjudication Procedure — consent and disclosure, screening scope by role and state, hit adjudication matrix, adverse action sequencing, 1033(e)(2) consent application and post-hire self-report duty

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance, the Chief HR Officer and Employment Counsel (FCRA and adverse action sections); re-approved annually and on any change to a state fingerprint requirement

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per hire — screening completed before contract execution or start date; FCRA pre-adverse action notice followed by a minimum 5 business day dispute window before a final decision; 1033(e)(2) consent application filed before any engagement in the business of insurance; producer self-report of a criminal or administrative action within 30 days of the event in most states

Deadline reminders configured.value: Screening queue alerts at day 5 and day 10 of an open screening, an alert on the final day of the FCRA dispute window, and a 30-day alert on any pending 1033(e)(2) consent application

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Signed FCRA disclosure and authorisation, 1033 questionnaire, screening report, fingerprint receipt, adjudication note and any 1033(e)(2) consent letter retained 7 years from the end of the relationship in a restricted-access store

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any producer or employee who transacted insurance business before screening cleared, or who is identified as a 1033 prohibited person without consent, is logged with the exposure period and the disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every 1033 prohibited-person determination, every decision to sponsor a 1033(e)(2) consent application and every separation driven by a 1033 finding

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every producer contracted and every employee hired into an insurance-transacting role in the quarter, plus every post-hire criminal or administrative action self-reported in the quarter

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — one person engaged in the business of insurance without a completed clearance, or a known 1033 prohibited person without written consent, is a fail and an immediate escalation to the Head of Compliance

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per hire; test runs quarterly over that quarter's hires and contracts with 100% review of every screening that returned a criminal or regulatory hit

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside Compliance screening and HR recruiting and must not have adjudicated any sampled screening

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly 1033 screening workpaper (hire and contract extract, screening trace, adjudication re-performance, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under Licensing / Screening, access-restricted

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Screening register with person, role, state, screening date, outcome and any 1033 consent reference, plus the adjudication notes, producible for a market conduct exam or a department 1033 enquiry within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Compliance Manager answers department 1033 and background enquiries; Regulatory Counsel owns any 1033(e)(2) consent correspondence with the domiciliary commissioner and any federal enquiry

checklist.step: Trigger screening at offer or contracting, before any start date
actions: Flag every requisition and every producer contracting request as insurance-transacting or not, using the role definition list agreed with Compliance.
On offer acceptance or contracting approval, raise the screening request with legal name, all former names, date of birth, address history and the states the person will transact in.
Set the candidate record to 'Screening pending' and record that no start date may be confirmed until clearance.
Send the request to Compliance the same day the offer is accepted so the screening does not run against the start date.
checklist.done: every insurance-transacting offer or contract raises a screening request on acceptance, with the record held at 'Screening pending'.

checklist.step: Capture the FCRA disclosure, authorisation and the 1033 questionnaire
actions: Send the standalone FCRA disclosure and the written authorisation for a consumer report as separate documents, not buried in the application form.
Send the 1033 questionnaire asking directly whether the person has ever been convicted of any felony involving dishonesty or a breach of trust, or any felony under Chapter 47 of Title 18.
Add the state-specific notices the person's state requires and any state consent for fingerprinting.
File the signed set against the person's record and refuse to open the screening without it.
checklist.done: signed FCRA disclosure, authorisation, 1033 questionnaire and state notices are on file before any screening is ordered.

checklist.step: Order the criminal background check to the right scope
actions: Order a search covering federal and state criminal records for every county of residence in the last 7 years, plus a national criminal database and sex offender registry search.
Add credit history only where the role handles premium funds and the state permits it, since some states restrict credit use in hiring.
Set the search to report the offence, the statute, the disposition, the disposition date and whether the offence is a felony or a misdemeanour.
Record the order reference and expected turnaround on the screening record and chase at day 5 if nothing has returned.
checklist.done: a scoped criminal search is ordered covering 7 years of county residence plus federal and national databases, with an order reference recorded.

checklist.step: Arrange fingerprinting where the state requires it for licensure
actions: Read the state's licensing page for whether fingerprints are required for a resident producer licence and which vendor the state designates.
Schedule the appointment and give the producer the state-specific fingerprint card or vendor code they must present.
Record the submission date and the state's transmission reference, and diary the FBI response at the state's stated turnaround.
Hold the licence application where the state will not act without the fingerprint result on file.
checklist.done: fingerprints are submitted through the state's designated vendor with the reference recorded and the response diarised.

checklist.step: Search regulatory and administrative action sources
actions: Pull the Producer Database report and read the regulatory actions section, which surfaces RIRS entries and, where available, Special Activities Database entries.
Search the person's name on each intended state department's enforcement action list for orders that predate their licensure.
For anyone selling variable products, search FINRA BrokerCheck for disclosures, and search the SEC action list where the role touches registered products.
Record every hit with its date, the issuing regulator, the conduct alleged and the order reference.
checklist.done: regulatory action searches across PDB, state enforcement lists and, where relevant, BrokerCheck are complete with every hit recorded at source.

checklist.step: Run sanctions and exclusion screening on the same record
actions: Screen the person against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list and the consolidated sanctions lists.
Screen against the relevant government exclusion and debarment lists for the lines the company writes.
Clear or escalate each potential match with a documented reason rather than closing on name similarity alone.
Record the screening date, the lists used and the outcome against the person's record.
checklist.done: sanctions and exclusion screening is complete with every potential match dispositioned in writing and the list versions recorded.

checklist.step: Adjudicate every hit against the 1033 matrix
actions: For each criminal hit determine three things from the record: is it a felony, does it involve dishonesty or a breach of trust, and what is the disposition date.
Apply the adjudication matrix: felony involving dishonesty or breach of trust equals 1033 prohibited absent written consent; other felonies and misdemeanours go to a documented individual assessment.
For regulatory hits assess whether the conduct would support licence denial under Model 218 section 12 in any intended state.
Write the determination, the facts relied on and the matrix cell applied onto the screening record, signed and dated.
checklist.done: every hit carries a dated written determination naming the felony test applied and the matrix outcome.

checklist.step: Run the FCRA adverse action sequence before any final decision
actions: Where the screening report may drive a decline, send the pre-adverse action notice with a copy of the report and the Summary of Rights before deciding.
Hold the decision open for at least 5 business days so the person can dispute inaccuracies with the consumer reporting agency.
Consider any dispute outcome or explanatory evidence and record it before finalising.
Send the final adverse action notice naming the agency, stating the agency did not make the decision, and file both notices with their dispatch dates.
checklist.done: both FCRA notices are evidenced with dispatch dates and a dispute window of at least 5 business days separates them.

checklist.step: Sponsor and track the 1033(e)(2) written consent application where one is needed
actions: Where the business case supports engaging a person with a disqualifying felony, prepare the 1033(e)(2) consent application to the insurance regulator of the state with jurisdiction.
Assemble the application: conviction record and disposition, rehabilitation evidence, the proposed role and its supervision, and the company's undertaking.
Submit it and record the submission date, the department contact and the reference, chasing at 30 days.
Keep the person out of any insurance-transacting activity until the written consent is granted and filed — a pending application is not consent.
checklist.done: a consent application is submitted and tracked, and the person performs no insurance-transacting work until the written consent is on file.

checklist.step: Release contracting or the start date only on a recorded clearance
actions: Set the screening outcome — Cleared, Cleared with conditions, Consent required, or Declined — on the HRIS and producer master record with the date and the adjudicator.
Release the start date or the producer agreement only on Cleared or on Cleared with conditions where the conditions are implemented.
Tell the hiring manager and the Agency Relations Manager in writing what the person may not do where conditions apply.
Never allow a provisional start pending screening on an insurance-transacting role.
checklist.done: the start date or contract issues only against a dated Cleared status recorded on HRIS and the producer master.

checklist.step: Extend the same gate to agency staff and third-party sellers
actions: Write into every agency, MGA and TPA agreement the obligation to screen their own insurance-transacting staff for 1033 disqualification and to attest annually.
Collect the annual attestation and record the attestation date and signatory against the counterparty record.
Sample-test attestations by requesting evidence for named individuals during the annual due diligence review.
Escalate any counterparty that cannot evidence screening to the Head of Compliance with a remediation deadline.
checklist.done: every distribution counterparty carries a contractual 1033 screening obligation and a dated annual attestation, sample-tested at due diligence.

checklist.step: Run the post-hire self-report and re-screen duty
actions: Publish the standing obligation for producers and staff to report any criminal charge, conviction or administrative action within 30 days of the event, matching the state licensing reporting duty.
Ingest the daily NIPR status change and regulatory action feed and open a case on every new action against an active producer.
Re-screen employees in insurance-transacting roles on the cycle the procedure sets and on any promotion into premium handling.
Route every post-hire hit straight to the adjudication step rather than treating it as a lower-priority query.
checklist.done: post-hire actions arrive by self-report and by the NIPR action feed, and each opens an adjudication case.

checklist.step: Suspend immediately where a 1033 prohibition is identified after engagement
actions: On identifying a prohibited person already engaged, remove all insurance-transacting duties and system access the same day.
Extract the business they transacted since the disqualifying event and quantify policies, premium and commission.
Decide with Regulatory Counsel whether to seek 1033(e)(2) consent or separate, and whether the state must be told.
Record the decision, the date and the notifications made on the case.
checklist.done: a prohibited person is removed from insurance duties the same day, with their transacted business quantified and a counsel-signed disposition.

checklist.step: Report screening outcomes and open cases to governance
actions: Log screening volumes, hit rates, declines, pending consents and open post-hire cases as a control metric in the GRC platform each month.
Report to the Compliance Committee quarterly with named open cases and their ageing, without exposing unnecessary personal detail.
Track remediation of any control failure — screening bypassed, adverse action mis-sequenced — to closure in the same platform.
Link the metric to the 1033 obligation record so the control coverage is visible in the regulatory inventory.
checklist.done: screening metrics and open cases are logged monthly in the GRC platform and reported quarterly with ageing.

checklist.step: Retain screening evidence securely for the full period
actions: Move signed disclosures, questionnaires, screening reports, fingerprint receipts, adjudication notes and consent letters into the restricted Licensing / Screening area of the evidence repository.
Apply a 7-years-from-end-of-relationship retention label and restrict access to Compliance, Employment Counsel and Audit by named role.
Confirm the access control list is reviewed at least annually and that downloads are logged.
Confirm the record is retrievable by person, screening date and outcome without exposing report content in the index.
checklist.done: screening files are retained 7 years past the relationship in a restricted store with logged access and an annually reviewed access list.

testing.step: Build the population of people who entered insurance-transacting roles in the quarter
actions: Extract every hire, internal transfer and rehire into a role flagged insurance-transacting, with start date and location state.
Extract every producer contract executed in the quarter from the agency/producer management system with NPN and contracting date.
Add every post-hire criminal or administrative action self-reported or received on the NIPR action feed in the quarter.
Reconcile hire counts to payroll starters and contract counts to executed agreements before sampling.
testing.done: the population covers hires, transfers, producer contracts and post-hire actions, reconciled to payroll and executed agreements.

testing.step: Reconcile every population row to a completed screening record
actions: Join the population to the screening register on person identifier and list every row with no screening record.
For matched rows compare the screening completion date to the start date or the contract execution date.
List every screening completed after engagement began as an automatic exception with the days of unscreened exposure.
Check the role flag itself — an insurance-transacting role mis-flagged as non-transacting is a systemic exception, not a single miss.
testing.done: every population row matches a screening completed before engagement, or is listed as an exception with the exposure days.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of screenings returning any criminal or regulatory hit and 100% of post-hire reported actions.
Take 25 clean screenings at random from the remainder using a recorded seed, minimum 40 records overall.
Record population size, seed, selection date and selector in the workpaper.
Handle the sample under restricted access, since the files carry criminal and personal data.
testing.done: a reproducible, access-restricted sample covering every hit and post-hire action is fixed and documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the screening scope check on each sampled record
actions: Read the screening report and confirm it actually covered every county of residence in the last 7 years, plus federal and national criminal databases.
Confirm all former names supplied by the person were searched, since an unsearched maiden or former name hides convictions.
Confirm fingerprinting was performed where the state required it and that the state result is on file.
Log any scope gap as an exception even where the report came back clear — a clear report on the wrong scope proves nothing.
testing.done: each sampled screening is confirmed to have covered the required counties, databases, former names and fingerprints, or the scope gap is logged.

testing.step: Re-perform the 1033 adjudication on every hit
actions: Read the court record or disposition document behind each hit rather than the vendor summary line.
Reach your own conclusion on the two statutory tests: is it a felony, and does it involve dishonesty or a breach of trust.
Compare to the recorded adjudication; a right outcome reached on the wrong test is still an exception.
Confirm that anyone concluded prohibited has either a granted 1033(e)(2) consent on file or no insurance-transacting activity at all.
testing.done: every hit has an independent felony and dishonesty determination, and every prohibited person has consent on file or no insurance activity.

testing.step: Test the FCRA adverse action sequencing
actions: For every declined candidate in the sample confirm a pre-adverse action notice with the report and Summary of Rights was sent before the decision.
Recompute the elapsed business days between the pre-adverse and final adverse notices and confirm at least 5.
Confirm the final notice names the consumer reporting agency and states the agency did not make the decision.
Log any decision communicated before the dispute window closed as a fail, regardless of the underlying conviction.
testing.done: every decline shows both notices with a recomputed dispute window of at least 5 business days and correct agency wording.

testing.step: Trace sampled clearances to the engagement gate
actions: For each sampled producer confirm the contract execution date is later than the recorded clearance date.
Pull applications and policies attributed to the producer and confirm none predates the clearance.
For employees, compare the HRIS start date and system access provisioning date to the clearance date.
Quantify any activity in the unscreened window in policies, premium and commission.
testing.done: no sampled person transacted insurance business before their recorded clearance date, or the activity is quantified.

testing.step: Test the third-party and post-hire monitoring controls
actions: Take 10 distribution counterparties and confirm the current agreement carries the 1033 screening obligation and a dated annual attestation.
Request underlying screening evidence for two named individuals per counterparty and confirm it exists.
Take one month of the NIPR regulatory action feed and trace every action against an active producer to an opened adjudication case within 2 business days.
Log counterparties unable to evidence screening and any action feed item with no case.
testing.done: 10 counterparties show a current obligation and attestation with evidence produced, and every action feed item traced to a case within 2 business days.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying the person reference (not the underlying conviction detail), role, state, screening date, engagement date and exposure days.
Assign a root cause from the standing list: role mis-flagged, screening ordered late, scope incomplete, adjudication test misapplied, adverse action mis-sequenced, counterparty attestation missing.
Set an owner and remediation date, and for prohibited-person findings record the counsel disposition reference.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has a privacy-appropriate issue with root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the pre-engagement screening completion rate and the adjudication accuracy rate and compare each to the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper reference behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who adjudicated none of the sampled screenings, sign the workpaper.
Report any prohibited-person finding to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the restricted area of the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with screening completion and adjudication accuracy rates, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed under restricted access.

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly roster reconciliation test workpaper (independent three-source rebuild, break re-classification, exposure recomputation, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under Licensing / Reconciliation

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Signed quarterly reconciliation report with break counts by class and state, the break register with dispositions and the underlying extracts, producible for a market conduct exam producer-licensing request within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager answers exam requests for the producer roster reconciliation; Regulatory Counsel clears any disclosure of business written outside a licence or appointment

checklist.step: Freeze the quarter and extract the internal producer roster
actions: Set the as-at date to the last calendar day of the quarter and take the extract within 5 business days of quarter end.
Export per producer per state: NPN, legal name, agency NPN, contract status, appointment status, appointment effective date, LOA authorised, termination date if any.
Include terminated producers whose termination date falls in the quarter, so departures are visible rather than filtered out.
Record the extract row count, the as-at date and the extractor on the reconciliation workbook cover sheet.
checklist.done: a dated as-at roster extract exists with per-state appointment and contract detail, including in-quarter terminations, with its row count recorded.

checklist.step: Pull the NIPR licence extract for every roster NPN
actions: Submit the roster NPN list to the NIPR bulk Producer Database service and download the response file the same day.
Take per NPN per state: licence class, status, LOA granted, issue date, expiration date and the appointment records NIPR holds for the company FEIN.
Confirm the response file returns a row for every NPN submitted and investigate any NPN NIPR does not recognise.
Save the response file dated as the licence-side source of truth for the reconciliation.
checklist.done: a dated NIPR bulk extract covers every roster NPN with licence and appointment detail, and unmatched NPNs are investigated.

checklist.step: Obtain the state-side appointment listings
actions: For each appointing state download the company's appointment listing — from the NIPR appointment report where the state supports it, otherwise from the state department's company portal.
Record for each state the listing date, the source used and the total appointment count the state shows.
Chase any state whose listing is unavailable and record the reason on the workbook so the coverage gap is explicit.
Never substitute the internal roster for a state listing when a state cannot be retrieved.
checklist.done: a dated appointment listing exists for every appointing state, or the retrieval gap is explicitly recorded with the reason.

checklist.step: Normalise the keys across the three sources
actions: Standardise the join key to NPN plus two-letter state code plus appointment type, and map the company identifier across sources on FEIN and NAIC co-code.
Normalise LOA codes to a single vocabulary, since state listings, NIPR and the producer master often name the same authority differently.
Resolve name-only rows by looking the NPN up in the PDB rather than fuzzy matching on name.
Log every normalisation rule applied so the reconciliation can be reproduced.
checklist.done: all three sources share a normalised NPN/state/type key and LOA vocabulary, with every mapping rule logged.

checklist.step: Run the three-way match and produce the break list
actions: Full-outer-join roster, NIPR licence data and state appointment listings on the normalised key.
Produce a matched count and a break count per state, and reconcile matched plus break to the total distinct keys so nothing is dropped.
Output the break list with every source's values side by side so the break can be read without re-querying.
Publish the counts to the workbook cover sheet before any classification begins.
checklist.done: the three-way match produces matched and break counts per state that foot to total distinct keys, with a side-by-side break list.

checklist.step: Classify every break into a named class
actions: Assign each break one class: appointed-but-unlicensed, licensed-and-writing-but-unappointed, internally-terminated-but-still-appointed, state-appointed-but-absent-from-roster, LOA mismatch, or duplicate NPN record.
Add the state, the NPN, the first date the break could have existed and the source combination that produced it.
Never leave a break unclassified as 'timing' without stating which transaction is in flight and its confirmation number.
Sort the register so the classes that carry regulatory exposure sit at the top.
checklist.done: every break carries a named class, a first-possible date and, where called timing, an in-flight transaction confirmation number.

checklist.step: Quantify the business exposure behind each break
actions: For each break pull applications, bound policies and endorsements attributed to that producer in that state during the break window.
Add commission paid in the window from the commission platform.
Record policy count, written premium and commission on the break register row so breaks are ranked by exposure, not by count.
Flag any break with in-force policies for immediate escalation regardless of its class.
checklist.done: every break row shows policy count, written premium and commission for its window, with in-force exposure flagged.

checklist.step: Route each break to an owner with a due date
actions: Open a case per break assigning the owner by class: Licensing Ops for missing appointments and terminations, Data Quality for master data breaks, Agency Relations for producers who have quietly left.
Set the due date at 15 business days from quarter end for regulatory-exposure classes and 30 for data-only classes.
Attach the side-by-side source evidence to the case so the owner does not have to re-derive the break.
Report open cases and their ageing weekly until the register closes.
checklist.done: every break has an owner, a class-appropriate due date and attached source evidence, with weekly ageing reporting.

checklist.step: File the missing appointments and terminations that the breaks reveal
actions: For licensed-and-writing-but-unappointed breaks verify the licence is Active, then submit the appointment transaction in NIPR and record the confirmation number and effective date.
For internally-terminated-but-still-appointed breaks submit the termination transaction with the correct termination effective date and reason code.
Where the termination effective date is more than 30 days past, treat it as a late filing and raise the tracker issue alongside the submission.
Update the break case with the confirmation number and close only when the next PDB pull shows the change.
checklist.done: every appointment and termination break has a submitted NIPR transaction with a confirmation number, closed only on PDB confirmation.

checklist.step: Cancel stale appointments before the state billing cut-off
actions: List every state-appointed producer with no contract, no roster record and no business written in the last 12 months.
Confirm with the Agency Relations Manager that the relationship is genuinely over before cancelling, since a dormant producer is not a departed one.
Submit the terminations and non-renewal instructions before each state's appointment renewal billing cut-off date.
Record the appointment fees avoided and report the figure to the Head of Distribution.
checklist.done: stale appointments are cancelled ahead of each state's billing cut-off with the fee saving quantified and reported.

checklist.step: Fix the data-quality root causes rather than the rows
actions: Group breaks by root cause: NPN missing or mistyped at onboarding, duplicate producer records, appointment status updated manually instead of from NIPR, LOA free-typed rather than picked from a list.
Raise a change request for each systemic cause, such as making NPN mandatory and format-validated at producer creation.
Merge duplicate producer records under a surviving NPN and repoint policies and commissions to the survivor.
Track the break count per cause quarter on quarter to prove the fix worked.
checklist.done: each systemic cause has a raised change request and a quarter-on-quarter break count trend proving whether it is reducing.

checklist.step: Reconcile commission payments to appointment validity
actions: Extract commission paid in the quarter by producer and state and join it to the appointment effective and termination dates.
List payments made where no appointment was in force on the transaction date and quantify the amount.
Route each to the Producer Compliance Manager for a clawback or accept decision, recorded in writing.
Feed confirmed appointment dates back into the commission engine so the same payment cannot recur.
checklist.done: every commission payment made outside an appointment window is quantified with a written clawback or accept decision.

checklist.step: Produce and sign the quarterly reconciliation report
actions: Publish the report: roster count, NIPR match rate, state appointment match rate, breaks by class and state, exposure by class, and open breaks carried forward with ageing.
State the coverage explicitly, naming any state whose listing could not be retrieved and what was done instead.
Sign the report as preparer and have the Distribution Operations Manager sign as reviewer.
Compare the break rate to the prior three quarters and comment on the trend.
checklist.done: a signed quarterly report shows match rates, breaks by class and state, exposure, carried-forward ageing and a four-quarter trend.

checklist.step: Table the results to distribution and compliance governance
actions: Present the reconciliation at the quarterly distribution governance meeting with the breaks that carry written business named individually.
Agree remediation owners and dates for anything still open beyond its due date and minute them.
Send the report to the Compliance Committee and flag any item requiring a regulatory notification decision.
Confirm at the next meeting that the prior quarter's agreed actions actually closed.
checklist.done: the reconciliation is tabled with named exposure breaks, minuted owners and dates, and prior-quarter closure confirmed.

checklist.step: Retain the reconciliation pack and carry open breaks forward
actions: File the workbook, the three dated source extracts, the break register with dispositions and the NIPR remediation confirmations under Licensing / Reconciliation / <quarter>.
Apply a 7-years-from-reconciliation retention label and confirm the pack is retrievable by quarter, state and NPN.
Copy every break still open at close into the next quarter's register with its original identification date so ageing is preserved.
Reconcile the filed pack's break count to the signed report before closing the quarter.
checklist.done: the reconciliation pack is retained under a 7-year label, open breaks carry forward with original ageing, and counts tie to the signed report.

testing.step: Rebuild the roster population independently from source
actions: Take your own as-at quarter-end extract of the producer master rather than using the team's workbook extract.
Compare your row count and NPN set to the team's extract and list any producer present in one and not the other.
Confirm in-quarter terminations are present in both, since filtering them out is the commonest way a reconciliation looks clean.
Record the comparison in the workpaper before proceeding.
testing.done: an independent roster extract is taken and reconciled row-for-row to the team's extract, with every difference listed.

testing.step: Test roster completeness against writing agents and commission payees
actions: Extract every distinct writing producer NPN on policies bound in the quarter and every distinct commission payee.
Join both to the roster and list any NPN that transacted or was paid but does not appear on the roster.
Compute the completeness variance as unmatched NPNs over total transacting NPNs and compare it to the 0.5% threshold.
A variance above threshold fails the reconciliation itself, because the population it ran on was incomplete.
testing.done: roster completeness is measured against writing agents and commission payees and compared to the 0.5% threshold.

testing.step: Draw and document the break sample
actions: Take 100% of breaks classified as carrying written business and 100% of breaks aged more than one quarter.
Take 25 further breaks at random across the remaining classes using a recorded seed, minimum 40 breaks overall.
Take an additional 20 matched (non-break) rows at random to test for breaks the match failed to detect.
Record population size, seed, selection date and selector in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all exposure and aged breaks plus a matched-row control sample is fixed and documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the three-way match on the sampled rows
actions: Pull the current PDB report for each sampled NPN and read the licence status, LOA and company appointment section yourself.
Open the relevant state appointment listing and locate the producer directly rather than relying on the workbook row.
Reach your own matched-or-break conclusion, and for the matched control sample confirm no break was missed.
Any difference between your conclusion and the register, in either direction, is an exception.
testing.done: each sampled row has an independent match conclusion drawn from the PDB and the state listing, including the matched control sample.

testing.step: Re-perform the break classification and re-derive the break window
actions: For each sampled break decide the class yourself from the three source values before reading the register's class.
Derive the break start date from the underlying event — licence expiry, termination effective date, first application date — not from the reconciliation run date.
Compare your class and window to the register and log every difference, since a mis-classed break is routed to the wrong owner.
Challenge every break called 'timing' by opening the claimed in-flight transaction confirmation in NIPR.
testing.done: each sampled break has an independently derived class and window, and every 'timing' claim is verified against a real NIPR transaction.

testing.step: Recompute the exposure behind the sampled breaks
actions: For each sampled break pull policies bound and endorsements issued in your derived window, by risk state.
Pull commission paid in the same window and recompute the totals.
Compare policy count, premium and commission to the register figures and log every material difference.
Where your window is wider than the register's, note the additional policies the register never counted.
testing.done: exposure is independently recomputed for every sampled break and reconciled to the register, with under-counted policies identified.

testing.step: Trace break remediation to a confirmed outcome
actions: For each closed sampled break open the recorded NIPR confirmation number and confirm the transaction exists with the right NPN, state and effective date.
Pull a current PDB report and confirm the appointment or termination now shows as expected.
Recompute days from break identification to remediation and compare to the 15 or 30 business day due date for its class.
Log any break closed on a case note with no confirmed transaction behind it as a fail.
testing.done: every closed sampled break traces to a confirmed NIPR transaction visible on the PDB, with remediation days recomputed against its due date.

testing.step: Test coverage, carry-forward and the stale appointment sweep
actions: Confirm an appointment listing was obtained for every appointing state and that any gap is named on the report rather than silently dropped.
Take the prior quarter's open breaks and confirm each appears in this quarter's register with its original identification date preserved.
Take the stale appointment cancellation list and confirm each cancellation was submitted before that state's billing cut-off, using the state invoice date.
Confirm no cancelled producer subsequently wrote business in that state.
testing.done: state coverage gaps are disclosed, prior-quarter breaks carry forward with original ageing, and every cancellation preceded its state billing cut-off.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying NPN, state, break class, derived window, recomputed exposure and remediation days.

Assign a root cause from the standing list: extract filtered, key normalisation wrong, break mis-classed, timing claim unsupported, remediation closed without confirmation, state listing not obtained.
Set an owner and remediation date, and where written business sat outside a licence or appointment record the counsel assessment reference.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue with recomputed exposure and remediation days, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the roster completeness variance, the break detection accuracy from the matched control sample and the on-time remediation rate.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper reference behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared no part of the reconciliation workbook, sign the workpaper.
Report unresolved breaks carrying written business to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with completeness variance, detection accuracy, on-time remediation rate, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed.
